posts.author: Dimestore
posts.body:
It's kind of a little experiment I'm doing, very avant'garde if I don't say so myself. The idea is that the game is 8 bit, just solid colors, very little detail (Won't get into it but it's just an experiment I'm tooling around with for fun)
What's the easiest way to generate the tilesets I need. Just basic colors, literally barebones. I just want to say, have the green tiles be grass you can walk around in, and dark green tiles to make trees or grey for rocks, blue for water, that you can't walk though, I know how to do that.
I was able to get my character sets by just going into the defaults and opening the image up in paint and just filling the entirerty of the walking sprites with a solid color square. So your character is a little red square running around.
But the tile sets I'm having some difficulty, I opened the defaults and they're all so complicated, I just tried randomly filling the like tiles (grass with brown rocks around it for example) but it just doesn't seem to translate right
Could I hypothetically just make one tile set the same size as a basic tile set, and just fill it with chucks of the color palattes I want to use and then set whats walkable and whats not inside the database in the actual game?

posts.author: Jollo
posts.body:
RPG Maker uses the tiles from the tilemap and takes certain parts of one tile to create different variations for certain situations (those are the auto-tiles). That's why appears to not translate right.
This explains how tilesets are organized:
Asset Standards
As you don't need the original tiles I would recommend to just take those chunks that belong together and fill them with the color of your choice.
Otherwise, you could also use "A5" for you own tileset in the database. A5 is for "normal" tiles without any auto-tiling.
